description: Wyoming-only rules checked against the compiled Wyoming Statutes in Title 31 and WYDOT Driver Services pages. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines. Wyoming does not publish a numeric demerit-point suspension total in the pages used here.

questions.q: Wyoming's 20 mph limit applies when passing a school building or grounds, or in a designated school zone or school crossing, if
options: The school is in session, whether or not a sign is posted
Appropriate signs giving notice of the reduced speed limit are erected
A school bus is loading anywhere in the county
questions.explanation: W.S. 31-5-301(b)(i) sets 20 miles per hour when passing a school building or its grounds, or within any other area near a school designated by an official traffic-control device as a school zone with a reduced speed limit, or a school crossing, if appropriate signs giving notice of the reduced speed limit are erected.

questions.q: The statutory maximum in a Wyoming urban district, residence district, or subdivision, other than a designated private road, is
questions.explanation: W.S. 31-5-301(b)(ii) sets 30 miles per hour in any urban district and in any residence district or subdivision, except on a road designated a private road under W.S. 18-5-306(a)(vii).

questions.q: Except where the superintendent designates a higher interstate limit, Wyoming's statutory maximum on interstate highways is
questions.explanation: W.S. 31-5-301(b)(iii) sets 75 miles per hour on interstate highways except as provided in paragraph (vi). Paragraph (vi) sets 80 miles per hour on interstate highways designated by the superintendent. Paragraph (iii) also says it does not authorize noncompliance with a posted interstate limit.

questions.q: Where Wyoming does not state another maximum, the limit is 65 mph on a paved road and
questions.explanation: W.S. 31-5-301(b)(iv) sets 65 miles per hour where the roadway is paved and 55 miles per hour where it is unpaved, for other locations for which this subsection does not specify a maximum. A non-interstate state highway is specified separately at 70 mph in paragraph (b)(vii), so it is not in this residual category.

questions.q: The statutory maximum in W.S. 31-5-301 for a Wyoming state highway that is not an interstate is
questions.explanation: W.S. 31-5-301(b)(vii) sets 70 miles per hour on state highways that are not interstate highways. Subsection (c) says those maximums may be altered as authorized in W.S. 31-5-302 and 31-5-303.

questions.q: WYDOT imposes an administrative per se suspension when a DWUI chemical test shows an alcohol concentration of
options: 0.02 percent or greater for every driver
questions.explanation: WYDOT's Driving Privilege Withdrawal summary says an administrative per se suspension is imposed when the driver has been arrested for DWUI and the chemical test shows an alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or greater.

questions.q: Outside the 65-to-75 mph posted band in W.S. 31-5-301(d), the statute keeps a speeding violation off the driving record when the violation is
options: Less than 6 mph over the posted limit
Less than 10 mph over on every road
Any speed under 80 mph on an unpaved road
Exactly 6 mph over the posted limit
questions.explanation: W.S. 31-5-301(d) also excludes from those abstracts and records a speeding violation of less than 6 mph over the posted speed limit in all other instances and zones. School-zone, construction-zone, and commercial-motor-vehicle speeding violations are excepted from that exclusion.

questions.q: A Wyoming intermediate permit requires the applicant to be 16 and to have held a learner's permit for at least
questions.explanation: WYDOT says an intermediate permit, called an I2C in Wyoming law, requires the applicant to be 16, to have held a learner's permit for at least 10 days, to have completed 50 actual driving hours including 10 hours of night driving, and to pass a driving-skills test. A driver under 17 who has not completed a driver-education course is not eligible for full driving privileges.

questions.q: The driving practice required for a Wyoming intermediate permit is
options: No logged hours if the permit was held for 10 days
questions.explanation: WYDOT says the intermediate-permit applicant must have completed 50 actual driving hours behind the wheel, including 10 hours of night driving. The certification form is on the WYDOT forms page.

questions.q: With a Wyoming intermediate permit, the driver may legally drive only between 5 a.m. and 11 p.m., and may not drive with
options: More than one unrelated passenger under 18
More than three passengers of any age
A parent in the front seat
questions.explanation: WYDOT says an intermediate-permit holder is not allowed to drive with more than one passenger under 18 who is not a member of the immediate family, that everyone must wear a seat belt, and that the holder can legally drive only between 5 a.m. and 11 p.m. Those restrictions do not apply if the front-seat passenger is 18 or older and holds a valid license with full driving privileges.

questions.q: In Wyoming, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Wyoming issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Wyoming car permit: 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Wyoming complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Wyoming requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: In Wyoming, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Wyoming, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

provenance.manual: Learner Permits - Wyoming Department of Transportation

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Wyoming not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Wyoming restricts provisional drivers from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: Wyoming new drivers: off the road 11 p.m. to 5 a.m..

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Wyoming car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Wyoming car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Wyoming, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Wyoming, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: Wyoming, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

questions.q: In Wyoming, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Wyoming sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Wyoming residential district?
questions.explanation: Wyoming sets 30 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Wyoming?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Wyoming can be posted up to 80 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Wyoming rural interstate: up to 80 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes Wyoming's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Only texting is banned for all drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
questions.explanation: Wyoming: only texting is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Wyoming?
options: Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Wyoming, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Wyoming left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

questions.q: How is Wyoming's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
questions.explanation: Wyoming seat belt enforcement is secondary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Wyoming?
questions.explanation: Wyoming requires a car seat or booster until 9 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Wyoming: car or booster seat until 9 years.

questions.q: What is Wyoming's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Wyoming requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $20,000.
